finding.claim: Password-change endpoint sets the account password to the hardcoded literal "hunter2" with no current-password or re-authentication check, so any holder of a valid session can take over the account. This is also a hardcoded credential in source.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to /settings/password (session theft, XSS, or CSRF; see F3).

trace.note: login_required inner wrapper checks 'uid' in session.
Password set to the literal "hunter2"; attacker-known value.

finding.guards_checked: login_required correctly returns 401 for anonymous users; endpoint takes no input so no injection surface. No current-password check, no step-up/re-auth, no user-chosen password, no strength validation, hardcoded credential violates org policy and weakens authentication.

verdict.guard_found: routes.py:42 @login_required, which is implemented at routes.py:8-16 and aborts with 401 at line 12 when "uid" is not in session. It only blocks anonymous requests; it does not stop a holder of a valid session. No current-password, re-authentication, or step-up check exists in change_password (routes.py:43-45).
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: change_password at routes.py:41-45 is guarded only by login_required (routes.py:8-16), which rejects anonymous requests but not an authenticated session, and it sets the password to the literal "hunter2" at routes.py:44 with no re-auth. Any session holder can therefore set a known password on the account, which persists beyond the session. The candidate's "hardcoded credential" wording is loose, since the literal is a value being written rather than a credential checked. The set_password body is a stub at routes.py:52-53, so the write itself is not visible here.
